documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR above range. No bleeding, one small bruise on the shin from the woodpile. Ate less over the holidays, he thinks. Per PCP: 2.5 mg on Mondays, 5 mg other days (32.5 mg/week). Recheck 2 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well overall. He feels fully recovered from the stroke and is driving locally again. Oncology scan in early February he says was unchanged; no letter from that visit has reached us. Back a bit worse in the cold, 5/10, still functional on the ER morphine.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregular rhythm. Neuro: symmetric strength, normal speech and gait. Lumbar paraspinal tenderness, no radicular signs. Feet fine.

A/P
- Chronic low back pain on long-term opioid: stable; heat and stretching; same dose. PDMP reviewed, agreement current.
- AF on warfarin with a high INR in January; dose lowered to 32.5 mg/week, missed the 2-week recheck, March check scheduled.
- History of stroke, HTN, DM2, CAD: no changes.
- Records request to oncology for the winter scan.
Physical in May.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No bleeding. Continue 32.5 mg/week. Recheck with the May physical.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, 72.

Independent, driving locally, small woodworking jobs. No falls. PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1. Hearing and vision adequate. Advance directive and proxy (wife) on file; reviewed, no changes.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregularly irregular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro: no deficits. Feet: sensation intact, pulses palpable.

Oncology letter for the winter scan still not received despite request; patient reports stable. Will ask again.

Plan: labs today. Vaccines current; fall flu and COVID. Medications unchanged. Written plan provided.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR below range. Garden salads every night now, he says. Per PCP back to 35 mg/week (5 mg daily) and keep the salads steady. Recheck 2 to 3 weeks.

documents.title: INR recheck reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Left voicemail reminding him the INR recheck is overdue; asked him to come any morning this week.

documents.title: Wife calling: second stroke
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called. Sunday he developed left-sided weakness and slurred speech again; ambulance to the regional hospital, where they gave him the clot-dissolving drug. Admitted. She said he never came in for the INR recheck after June. PCP made aware.

reports.text: Non-contrast CT head. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. No acute territorial hypodensity. Ventricles normal for age.

Emergent non-contrast CT head for decline in alertness. Comparison 07/27/2025. Evolving acute infarct in the right cerebral hemisphere with surrounding edema and mild local mass effect. No midline shift. No hemorrhage. Ventricles unchanged.
reports.conclusion: Evolving right hemisphere infarct with edema and mild mass effect. No hemorrhage.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary, neurology
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, neurology service. Admitted 07/27/2025, discharged 08/06/2025 to inpatient rehabilitation.

72 year old man with atrial fibrillation on warfarin and an ischemic stroke with similar symptoms in 2024, brought in with left-sided weakness and slurred speech of three hours' duration.
Arrival: BP 170/95, HR 92 and irregular, afebrile. Left facial droop, left arm and leg drift, dysarthria.
Non-contrast CT head: no hemorrhage or mass effect. INR 1.5.
IV alteplase given.

Course: about 48 hours later he became increasingly drowsy and confused, with worse left-sided weakness. Vitals then BP 155/85, HR 88, temperature 37.1 C. Emergent CT head: evolving right hemisphere infarct with edema and mild local mass effect, no hemorrhage. Transferred to the neuro ICU, head of bed elevated, close neuro checks; alertness improved over the following days without further intervention. Returned to the stroke unit.
Warfarin restarted 08/04 with INR monitoring; aspirin and atorvastatin continued.

Diagnosis: recurrent acute ischemic stroke, right hemisphere, cardioembolic with subtherapeutic INR.
At discharge: alert, speech mildly slurred and improving, mild left-sided weakness, walking with therapy.
Discharge medications: warfarin (dose per INR), aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, morphine sulfate ER 30 mg twice daily. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP after rehab discharge; stroke clinic 3 months.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit, recurrent stroke
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit. Second ischemic stroke 7/27 with alteplase, then a period of drowsiness from swelling around the stroke on day 2, neuro ICU for a few days; hospital discharge 8/6 to inpatient rehab, home 8/20. Hospital summary reviewed; nothing yet from rehab. Wife with him.

Now: walks on his own but slower and more carefully, left leg tires. Left hand weaker than last year. Speech a little thick when tired. No headache. Mood: frustrated but not down.

Meds reconciled with the hospital list: warfarin, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, morphine ER 30 q12h. No changes.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregular rhythm. Mild left facial weakness. Mild dysarthria. Left arm and leg 4+/5, right 5/5. Gait slow, steady, no device.

A/P
- Recurrent ischemic stroke, right hemisphere, with mild residual left-sided weakness. Outpatient PT/OT/speech referrals were set by rehab. Stroke clinic in fall.
- AF on warfarin: INR at the last check before this stroke was low and the recheck was missed. INR checks every 2 weeks for now; RN to call if a check is missed.
- HTN, DM2, CAD, chronic pain: unchanged.
- No driving for now.
Follow up 3 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Two-week checks continue. Wife manages the pill box. In outpatient therapy twice a week.

documents.title: INR and vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. High-dose flu and this season's COVID vaccine, one in each arm, pressure held. Moving to every-4-week checks per PCP after three in-range results.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 10/14/2025. Corrected acuity 20/30 each eye. No diabetic retinopathy. Mild cataracts unchanged. Confrontation fields full. Return in one year. Medication list includes warfarin. NKDA.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Therapy finished last month. Walking around the block daily with his wife. Left side still a little weaker but he manages everything at home. Speech clear unless tired. Oncology: scan in October unchanged per patient.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregular rhythm. Mild left arm and leg weakness, gait steady and unaided.

A/P
- Recurrent ischemic stroke with mild residual left weakness: home exercises.
- AF on warfarin: INR monthly, in range lately.
- DM2, HTN, CAD: labs today, no changes.
- Chronic pain on long-term morphine: unchanged, PDMP reviewed.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No bleeding. Continue 35 mg/week. Next check mid-January.
